title: Printing & Stamping
strapline: Press, lift, and there it is — again and again.
intent: Printing is instantly rewarding — press, lift, and a mark appears — so every child gets a real result and wants to repeat it.
Repeating a print is early pattern-making: the same shape, over and over, in a line or a rhythm.
Exploring what different objects leave behind builds close looking and a first understanding of shape and texture.
Loading, pressing and lifting refines finger control and a careful, deliberate hand.
Choosing objects, colours and arrangements is genuine creative decision-making.
implementation: Offer paint in shallow trays and a big collection of printable objects — sponges, corks, blocks, leaves, cotton reels, hands.
Model the action — load, press firmly, lift straight up — and then step back.
Notice and name what's happening: 'You pressed the same shape three times — that's a pattern!'
Introduce repeating and comparing: 'What happens if you print the leaf, then the cork, then the leaf again?'
Let children explore freely first, then offer gentle challenges — a border, a repeating stripe, a print of their name's first letter.
Add natural and found objects to widen the marks and link to the outdoors.
Value the exploring over a neat picture — the learning is in the pressing and comparing.
key_questions: What kind of mark do you think this object will make?
Can you make a pattern — the same shape again and again?
Which object left your favourite print? What does it look like?
What happens if you press harder, or use more paint?
How could you carry on your pattern all the way along?

impact.text: Children explore paint, colour and printing tools freely, discovering the marks different objects make.
Children copy, continue and create repeating patterns as they print the same shapes in sequence.
Children load, press and lift with careful, controlled fingers and hands.
Children look closely and compare the prints, describing shape, texture and colour.
Children choose objects, colours and arrangements, making their own creative decisions.
Children make deliberate marks and early shapes, an important step towards writing.

enhancements: A big collection of printing objects: sponges, corks, blocks, cotton reels, bubble wrap.
Natural finds — leaves, shells, cut fruit and vegetables — for printing.
Home-made stamps from foam shapes stuck onto blocks.
Rollers, textured mats and different papers to print onto.
A pattern strip to continue, or a border to print around.
Ink pads and letter/number stamps linked to name-writing.

playing_exploring: Children explore what every object can do and get an instant, repeatable result.
They test pressing harder, softer, wetter and drier.
active_learning: Children repeat and refine their prints, staying with the pattern they are making.
creating_thinking: Children choose, arrange and combine prints, and work out how to continue a pattern.
